speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me understand your condition better, how long have these symptoms been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome (IC/BPS).

The combination of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, urgency, frequency, and dyspareunia (painful intercourse) strongly suggests Interstitial Cystitis. To confirm this and rule out other causes like UTIs or stones, I will need to see the results of a Urinalysis and a Cystoscopy. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis; REQUEST IMAGES: Cystoscopy.
